utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ruez, can you then tell me, how many were there killed in combat while a column was breaking through from Srebrenica to Kladanj, through the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't, for the simple reason that the exhumation process of some of these graves that we know are linked with the execution process are not exhumed yet, so we cannot say how many people in total have been assassinated since we have not finalised the exhumation process at this point still in 2010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes. When you say -- thank you, Judge. When you say the exhumation has not been finalised, do you mean it is continuing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope it is. Since 2001, this process is under the responsibility of BiH, and it goes at a very, very slow pace since nine years, though all the sites had been handed over, with all the necessary details, to the Bosnian authorities in 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, as you arrived at information about these places, ambushes and so on, generally through witnesses, can you tell us what those witnesses said, and how many they say were killed in the ambushes, so that we at least have a figure if we don't have the exhumations, themselves? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I won't be able to do that because, again, whatever numbers these witnesses would talk about have no scientific basis, since these are people who were in very stressful situations, and the instinct in that case when people recall the event is to inflate numbers. So I won't be able to give you any precise number about this, and this is probably a number that anyone will have a hard time to figure out extremely precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you investigated this matter, so can you tell this Trial Chamber what the number is, what the figure is? And then they can assess whether the number has been increased due to the psychological weakness of individuals or something else. And if you can't tell me, perhaps you can tell them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object. This has been asked and answered several times. It's an area that's really not in contest. The Prosecution's case has been the same since the Krstic matter, and we have barely scratched the surface, and we have a lot of time left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I confirm that I can only repeat, hour after hour, that the only data we rely on is the number of people who we find in the graves. We give a courtesy to the Defence to consider that any other body found on the surface died in a combat situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Tolimir, the witness has given you this answer several times, and you perhaps should consider to move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in my indictment there is a figure there, the number of people that I'm being accused of. Now, how am I going to deal with this if the investigators who took the statements from these people and took part in the events can't tell me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you got the relevant answers by this witness. You can deal with this with several witnesses in this trial. Wait for those who are able to answer these questions. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, I'm interested in whether there are any forensic -- there is any forensic evidence about these victims of combat, that is to say, those people who were killed in combat. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will have to leave this part of the cross-examination to the pathologist who dealt with the analysis and examination of these bodies. This was not part of my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, let's move on from this interview and go on to the statement you gave to the French Parliamentary Commission on the 22nd of February, 2001. And for that, may we call up 1D59, please. Thank you. We have the document on our screens now. May we turn to page 2, please. It is the penultimate paragraph on page 2 in the English, and it's also on page 2 of the Serbian. Thank you. The one-but-last paragraph. In this statement, you say as follows, and I'm quoting: "During that time, the line of people continued. There was extremely violent fighting with the Serbian forces who tried to ambush them along the way. At one point, part of the line left to make believe that there was an attack on Zvornik expressly to ease the pressure on the rest of the line. The greatest number of prisoners were taken during the day of the 13th of July." Now, my question to you is this: In your statement before the French Parliament, you talk about fierce clashes. Unfortunately, when there are fierce clashes, there are a lot of dead and wounded. Now, can you tell me, since you have been dealing with people on the list of killed, how many people were killed during these fierce clashes, thank you, or violent fighting?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, two things on this. First, about the clashes, again, since the military operation was not the aim of the testimony, this paragraph is to indicate the context. So, in fact, the context, if you break down this little paragraph, would be the ambushes at the start of a column. And then, indeed, once the column arrived in the area of Zvornik, as you know, there was intensive fighting, the column could even have stormed into Zvornik. A lot of people were called back from their activities to go on the front-line. The Zvornik Brigade was stripped of most of its numbers because they were going down to Zepa, and, indeed, we learned later on that a little part of the main column made a fake move towards Zvornik in order to distract the Serb forces from the point where they intended to exit. So, again, this is a small paragraph to indicate the context, but it's not the heart of the -- I hate calling this "the story." I mean, the concern of this case. And, again, I repeat, no way for me to give any figure regarding those killed in action. I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. And do you know the number of people killed in action? I know you can't give us a number, but do you know it, did you investigate?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think I have answered this question maybe probably more than 10 times since the beginning of this afternoon. No, I don't know. No, I cannot say. Until we have not finalised the entire exhumation process, no one will ever be able to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, if the witness knew he had to tell that in court, and he says he doesn't know. Please, don't repeat again this question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. But those who survived state this in their statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, could you tell me whether a military operation was one where part of the forces, as you say, tried to simulate an attack on Zvornik and changed direction?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Though it is not part of the investigation, this is something that we learned had happened, yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, may we have onto our screens 1D600 back again, please, or, rather, 1D60. 1D60 and page 3 of that document, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the document we just had on the screen, do you tender that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, I'd like to tender it, but we're going to use it some more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we can deal with that later. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Is he offering the entire testimony in front of the French Parliamentary? That's quite a bit. I would object to that. I'm not sure if that's necessary. For the same reasons as I've said before, if statements such as this come in, 92 bis or other -- there are other ways of bringing it in, but not the entire parliamentary statement just based on some short cross-examination pieces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir indicated that he will use this document later with this witness, and we will wait for having seen the relevant parts and then we will deal with that. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. That's right, we will be dealing with it some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'd like to dwell now for a moment on that same page. It's page 3, actually. I said 1D60, page 3 in Serbian. The last sentence in the middle column, paragraph 1, and I quote: "When we complete all the exhumations, we'll have, more or less, the number of those killed." And then in the next paragraph, you refer to one of the graves that we mentioned here, the Glogova grave, and you say, and I quote: "There is a specific feature. One of the graves in Glogova contains the bodies of people who were killed along the Konjevic Polje-Kravica road. The Serbs will say of them that they were killed in battle, whereas they were killed as soon as they set foot on the asphalt road." End of quotation, and we will add that to the total number. Now, what date are you talking about here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about 13 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, can you tell us how many bodies were buried in Glogova? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That will be a question to address to Professor Richard Wright, who has all the figures, in terms of numbers. But, again, for Glogova, there will be a need first to exhume all the sites who are south of Srebrenica. And as far as I know, aside the one that was exhumed by the ICTY probably in 2000, or latest in 1999, I don't think any of the sites that we have spotted south of Srebrenica have been exhumed so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. I'm not asking about other ones. I'm asking you specifically about Glogova. Can you tell us something and answer my question just with respect to Glogova, what the number was? I didn't ask you how many there were in the primary and secondary graves, but what the number was here, Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, General, I did answer your question. I said that I cannot answer it. This one will be answered by Professor Richard Wright.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Can you tell me, if one group is armed and is breaking through the encirclement and refuses to surrender, does that group then represent a legitimate target to attack or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a legitimate target. This is the reason why we have not taken into account any testimony of a person who would say that before being shot, they had not surrendered, had not handed over their weapons or threw them away. We consider these situations as combat situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Could you tell me whether all the ambushes for the opposite side, the combatants of the opposite side, was that legitimate too, a legitimate object and target of the two warring parties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. This is both asked and answered, and it's really calling for legal opinion, as well as we get into what's legitimate and what's not legitimate, which this witness has also indicated he's not prepared to be able to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. McCloskey, you are absolutely right. The witness is not here to answer legal questions. Please take that into account and carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you consider that a knowledge of combat theory is indispensable for one to conclude whether something is a combat situation or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I feel so incompetent in that matter that this is the reason why we focused only to determine the fate of people who had surrendered or had been captured and were under detention under the control of the security branch of the Bosnian Serb Army. These are the only ones this investigation had the duty to determine what happened to them, where they had been killed, where they had been buried, and later on where their bodies had been transported to in order to hide the evidence of that crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I asked you that so that I could see on the basis of what parameters you identified whether somebody in a mass grave -- whether people in a mass grave were killed through combat or not, and whether they had taken to the woods, and so on. And you took statements from people, and you judged by the locations, themselves? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the witness has indicated several times in which way he was able to investigate the facts, and you should proceed with questions related to the facts the witness can testify about. Please ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, it is not my intention to take away or add anything to your testimony. My only aim is to arrive at the truth before this Trial Chamber about the events which you investigated. So, if possible, could you please answer my next question bearing that in mind. Let's stay with page 2 -- or, rather, it's page 3 of 1D60, where you state the following: You say that you relied on a list supplied by the ICRC, and add: "The number of dead remains, now we know, after so many years, that all of them are missing and dead. That is not contentious anymore." Now, in another place of that same document, 1D60, the first part of your interview you say as follows: "The figure that we give is a minimum of the minimum. And whenever we quote figures, we know that hundreds are missing, but we would rather err on the side of caution and quote a lower number than a higher number." Now, my question to you is this: Can you tell us where -- well, we had the opportunity of reading in many places, in many reports provided to us by the Prosecution, this conservative attitude to numbers. How is it in evidence? Can you tell us whether you know that a number of Muslims from Srebrenica, after the fall of Srebrenica, crossed illegally to territory outside Bosnia-Herzegovina - Germany, Holland, and other third countries - and did you register them and strike them from the list of missing persons? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this, there is the testimony of an expert who testified on this demography aspect during the Krstic trial, so I won't enter in that field. But, again, all this is right. The figure that we bring up is very conservative. When, in any other press statement, you always read this figure of 8.000 as having been killed, we always say, no, the real number that we take in account is the number that will be known when the exhumation process is finished, and for sure this figure will be lower than the number of missing since we consider that a part of these have been killed, let's say, in combat.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Ruez, whether your investigative team or you knew that a number of men had left Srebrenica and Bosnia and Herzegovina to third countries in Western Europe and that they are still listed under missing persons and those killed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. Again, the expert, the demographer, would be able to give more details on this. What we knew at that time is that, indeed, one group of an unknown number crossed the Drina to try to find shelter in Serbia, but -- according to the information we received, was that there was nothing, let's say, ugly to report about their fates. The reason why, these people again are not -- were not part of the investigation. But I have no idea if some of them are not on the missing list, still on the list of missing, and if they are ever been reported as missing, since they were not missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, then, if you did know, by any chance, would then their names have to be struck off this list of missing persons of Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is the responsibility of the ICRC, who drafted this list, to then continue to deal with this list and update the list if someone shows up alive somewhere. But I cannot answer in the name of ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not asking you to answer on behalf of the ICRC. I'm just asking you this: If, as an investigator, you learned that some of these people were registered in third foreign countries, would you then request that their names be taken off the missing persons list for Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the witness has just answered this question. It's not necessary to repeat that. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, but I wasn't asking about whether the ICRC had to strike these names off the list, but rather whether the investigators would have to do it. Thank you, but I did not get an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the answer is always the same. The answer is that -- I mean, I have not read your indictment, General, but I don't believe that the Prosecution charges you with any missing person. I think the indictment, like it has always been, is focused only on the fact that several thousand persons who were prisoners have been murdered. The final number, again, today is still unknown, since we have still several secondary sites containing an unknown number of bodies that can be connected with the primary sites needs to be exhumed. So I cannot enter a debate about this missing list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. For your information, I am charged with genocide as well, and I have to try and shed light from every angle regarding -- including the things that you investigated. Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown 1D102. We can wait for it to come up on the monitors. In the meantime, let me just say that this is a newspaper report that caused a lot of excitement, and it was a statement by Mr. Tokaca, the director of the investigative centre, who, on the 21st of March, 2010, only a day after your evidence in this case, made public the following information. And I will just read the relevant portions. This report was published in all the daily papers and many weekly magazines in Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We don't have the document before us yet. I can't see the first page. We can only see here where it says the director of the Investigating Centre from Sarajevo, Mr. Mirsad Tokaca, said "yesterday" in Banja Luka, that in the course of the investigation of war crimes, he learned that about 500 people from Srebrenica were still alive, and yet their names are on the list of those missing in Srebrenica in July 1995. So he said that in the course of the investigation that he conducted, he learned that 500 people who were on the missing persons list for Srebrenica were still alive, and he also says: "We learned that about 70 persons who were buried at the Memorial Centre in Potocari were not in Srebrenica at the time at all."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I received information that this is the only page of this document, and I'm not sure if you have up-loaded this document in e-court. We have nothing except this page, and, therefore, you should be careful with that. You're not giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will read what you can see on the screen, and you will see that everything I have said is contained in there. I only mention this for the witness by way of introduction. It says the following, I quote: "Over 500 allegedly killed in Srebrenica still living."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there is a long quotation already in the transcript. I think you should now put a question to the witness. It's more appropriate to get information from this witness that's not just repetitive --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you tell us, please, whether in the meantime you have been informed of this, as reported by Mr. Tokaca in several press conferences that he gave both in Sarajevo and in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is, no, I was not aware that Mr. Tokaca gave these statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Can you tell us now, please, whether you know and whether the Prosecution knows that 500 people who are still living are listed as missing or killed in Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only answer for myself, and my answer is I discover these statements that were made by Mr. Tokaca. I cannot say for anyone other than myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ruez, can you then tell us if this is the first time that you hear of this, that Mr. Tokaca, who is a Muslim and lives in Sarajevo, and who is officially the director of that centre, and whose claim has not been disproved by anyone, can you tell us whether you are going to request these 500 individuals that he is mentioning here will be taken off the list? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'd like to hear the answer of the witness. He will be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the answer is very simple. I left the Tribunal in 2001. I have absolutely no authority -- for sure, I would not have the authority to retrieve anything from the records, and I have no authority to influence anyone to further investigate this matter. I'm no more part of the investigation team since nine years now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, I object to the last question because he states that it's not this -- something to the effect that there's been nothing to dispute that, when I'm sure the general knows in the press there has been, and I won't get into the details of it, but something that's absolutely contrary to that by the very person that's supposedly quoted. And by asking a question in this way, he is, out of the press or deliberately misleading the Court, and he shouldn't be doing either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't have any document on the screen or in e-court, and, therefore, I think your position is quite clear. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, is it true that almost no one, except partially this Centre for Documentation and Investigation, no one is really investigating whether persons who are on the missing persons list are still living and perhaps living somewhere in the West, Western Europe or the United States? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think it is not necessary to repeat and repeat and repeat. Otherwise, will you get always the same answers. The witness made very clear that he is no longer -- for many years no longer an employee of the OTP. He is not investigating anything further, so that you shouldn't continue putting these kind of questions to this witness. I think we must have the second break now. You should think about that, consider the guidance of the Chamber, and perhaps you can discuss it with your legal assistant. We adjourn and resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber was not aware -- before the break was not aware of the fact that the Defence notified this afternoon the document 1D00102, but only one page. This is perhaps one of the -- one reason for the confusion which took place before the break. The Chamber is of the view that if you want to have this page again on the screen and to read this portion - we can follow on the screen - in B/C/S into the transcript and put a question to that, you should do that, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we then please see on the screens that document that you just mentioned, the statement by Mr. Tokaca. Thank you. For the transcript, would you allow me to read the statement, because we will seek to tender it. Thank you. I'm reading a statement by Mirsad Tokaca, the director of the Research and Documentation Centre from Sarajevo: "Director of the Investigation and Research Centre from Sarajevo said yesterday in Banja Luka that in the course of the investigations into war crimes, he received information about 500 men from Srebrenica who are still living and who are on the list of those killed in Srebrenica in July of 1995." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you know that this statement was -- or gave rise to a debate in a session of the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have absolutely no clue about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you answer one more question. Do you know that the president of Republika Srpska - and tomorrow I will provide his statement - asked that this number be deducted from the number of the total -- from the total number of victims of Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about such a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether the person who now does the work that you did, investigating Srebrenica, should he seek to obtain these documents from the Centre for Investigating War Crimes in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no word to say about an investigation I am no longer a part of since nine years now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. My question is: Would it be necessary to obtain this statement given by an official organ for the cases still being tried here before this Tribunal? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a private person, and for the sake of historical purposes, I could just invite you to ask Mr. Tokaca to come to The Hague as a Defence witness. More than that I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. I was only asking whether the person who came to do your job, once you left, is that person capable of obtaining those documents or not? In other words, can an investigator have access to the documents possessed by the sides that are investigating these crimes?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I'm no longer in a position to provide an answer on this. I have to say that this is no longer my business, and I have no idea on the current investigative powers of the Office of the Prosecutor, and I have no word to say on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Can you tell us, then, while you were still in this job, were you able to co-operate with the investigating organs of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have done it. I didn't do it on purpose, aside of a statement analysis that we did based on these compilations obtained by the MUP and the Bosniak commission. In order to keep our independence, we had absolutely no longer contacts with them, aside for the police to organise materially some interview places and have maybe sometimes police vehicles to bring these people to -- for our interview process. But we, on purpose, disconnected from the work of this commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. The individuals concerned that are on the list provided by the ICRC as missing persons, would it be normal, once one learned that they were still living, that this information be made public? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I leave to Mr. Tokaca the responsibility of what he says to the press. The only thing I can say is that at least if this is correct, these people will not be identified through their DNA as being found in the mass graves we are concerned with. That's the only thing I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. I understand what you're saying. In order not to dwell on this anymore and not to waste any time, we will provide and present to you tomorrow some documents, such as, for instance, a statement by the prime minister. But for now, we'll move on to another question. Your book contains a large number of aerial photos that you were given by the American intelligence services. That's what you said here. Before I put a question to you, I would like to show you the statement that you provided to the French media. Could we please see 1D0159. This is an interview with the commissioner, Jean-Rene Ruez, leader of the investigating team into Srebrenica, provided in 2001. Could we please see page 11 of this document, a report to the Parliamentary Committee of France. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please give us the number again. This can't be the correct number, 1D0159.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D059. I apologise if I misspoke the first time. Thank you. 1D059.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To clarify, Mr. Ruez never said that this was provided by the intelligence services. He said the State Department, and there's a big difference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. We'll take a look at the text now and see what was said, and the witness can answer the question and take into account your remarks too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, we have page 11 -- can we have page 11, because I'd like to quote from that page. What paragraph is it? It's the third paragraph in the Serbian, and paragraph 5 in the English. With respect to the photograph which the USA sent you, you state, among other things: "We don't possess photographs at all showing the execution taking [Realtime transcript read in error "took"] place, if that is what you wish to know. We always have photographs showing before and after." Did I quote that correctly, and did you say that before the French Parliamentary Committee?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now may we show one of those photographs to the witness, which is 65 ter 01450, page 31, a Prosecution document. It's a photograph showing buses by the Nova Kasaba. Thank you. We haven't got the photograph -- yes, we have. It's just appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, you say that this was taken on the 13th of July, 1995. Tell us how you established the date at which the photograph was taken. It even says "1400 hours" there, "the 13th of July, 1995, 1400 hours." How did you establish the date and the time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to point a mistake in the transcript of my previous answer, when I said: "Yes, correct," but there was something mis-written. What I said is we never got a photograph of ongoing execution, not execution locations. It's an ongoing execution. The photos are before and after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this one and on your question, the markings that are on the picture, the yellow markings are my markings. The markings in the white boxes are original markings that were on the photograph, as provided by the State Department. So these dates are the dates these pictures were officially taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me on what basis you were able to establish that, or were you told that that was the date and time that the photograph was taken? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have -- I have no mean to control the origin of the markings. The interesting point for me, as an investigator, with this photograph is to confirm the statements of those who have been on this field, of those who were passing by by bus, and this matches the date of the picture. And probably even with the shadows of the buses, you could probably have a correct assessment of the hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So that means you can't tell the Trial Chamber how the date and time came to be written there of this photograph? You can or you cannot ? You cannot. Now let's look at photograph 31, please, 30 and 31. 30 and 31 next, please, from that same set. Could you tell the Trial Chamber how you were able to establish the date and time here too? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly the same answer. All what is in the white boxes has been put on it by the providers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Can you tell me whether the photographs were in colour or black and white, the ones you received? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, these photographs, are they the only ones of Nova Kasaba or were you offered some others, too, depicting Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the photographs that have been shown so far during the various trials are photographs that we have obtained on request. They have never been provided, without a previous request, from us. And, indeed, in the area of Nova Kasaba, since we were also looking for one execution site and mass graves, we received additional pictures connected with Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, can you tell us whether these photographs, the ones you've just shown us of this field, are identical to the situation as it was then, and were there any changes that were made compared to 2001, when you were the investigator?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are exactly the pictures that I got through the State Department at the time we requested for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you indicate to us where you see the convoy here, when this is a column, a mixed column of vehicles, small and large vehicles? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, in this picture, which is an instantaneous picture, the only thing you can see on the road is four buses driving in the direction -- or opposite the direction of this soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see some small cars next to the buses as well? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. At the bottom right of the picture, there is one on the road. There is also one parked alongside of the road when you go up, behind the -- at the corner behind one of the buses. And at the top left of the picture, you also have one vehicle on the road.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, may we have on e-court -- well, can we have the left of the photograph, where it says "Nova Kasaba, the 13th of July, 1995," can we show that on the left-hand side, and on the right-hand side can we have D28? And it's an exhibit introduced into evidence during witness testimony. It also shows Nova Kasaba the 13th of July, 1995, at 1400 hours. Thank you. It was testimony of the 26th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir repeat the numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- with the witness statement. He confirmed having given the statement, and he drew this in. He drew the markings by his own hand, the one we can see on the right-hand side of the page. And I'd like to quote from his statement, and then I'll ask you the question: "I sat together --" And the transcript page is 1383, lines 19 to 25 of the transcript. He says: "I sat together with other prisoners for some 20 minutes, and then I saw Ratko Mladic coming out of a combat vehicle. That was on the 13th of July, sometime between 1400 hours and 1445 hours." On page 1384, lines 4 to 6, he says the following: The witness said that that was correct, as shown here, and that the stadium was full. Now, I don't want to go through the whole statement, but at 1387 of the transcript, the witness marked the positions where the prisoners were. Now, in your testimony, Mr. Ruez, you said the following: You said that you're 100 per cent certain that with respect to this photograph, that the prisoners were in this field. And on page 930, lines 9 to 12, you said, and I quote: "For me, this is 100 per cent certain, because I can even see the guards here." Now, the witness marked the photograph and the place where the prisoners were located. He used a red pen to mark in that area, because we asked him whether there were a lot of them and he marked the area where the prisoners were located in red. And also with a red pen, he circled almost the entire stadium. According to him, General Mladic and the place where the guards were was in the upper left-hand corner, and he put a number 2 where that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question reads as follows: Can you explain to us whether, through witness testimony, you checked out the authenticity of the photographs sent you by the US authorities? You said the State Department, I believe. And how do you explain the fact that -- or, rather, the difference in the witness statement and what we see on the photograph? Because on the photograph we see, on the left-hand side of the football field, there's a group of prisoners, and in front of that group there's another group of persons, allegedly, whereas the witness drew this red area and said that the prisoners were in that whole area.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your question. To me, there were two informations. The one that can be seen on the picture and the testimony of the witness are not necessarily in conflict for a simple reason. It is that the picture -- the aerial imagery is an instant moment, at that moment pinpointed at 1400, but this is a situation of evolution. Maybe before 1400 there were more people on this field, but, anyhow, after 1400 there were suddenly more people because this place was getting more and more crowded during the surrender process. So the timing given by the witness said it was between -- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should switch off the microphone for any discussion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I remember having read that he described the situation that was around this hour. He says 1445. I'm not certain he was watching his watch at that moment that day, but again the situation in this location, that is, one main regroupment [sic] spot for captured prisoners and those who were surrendering, it was an evolution, so we only have one picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Could you tell us now -- well, the witness said that at 1400 hours he saw General Mladic and that the stadium was full. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get a citation of where that's being said so we can check it? Thank you, I've found it. It's in a witness statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that that was page 1383, lines 19 to 25. The witness said: "I was sitting together with some other prisoners for some 20 minutes." It was on the 13th of July, between 1400 hours and 1430 hours. I think that you have now been able to find that in English. Have you? The witness confirms his statement at transcript page 1384, line 4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: Is it possible to have this difference; that is to say, to have this difference between the photograph on the left and the photograph on the right, which the witness has drawn in red, whereas the photograph on the left just shows a small amount of people to the left of the football field compared to those sitting in front? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say for sure, since I was not an eye-witness that day at that hour. But one thing is sure, that it is that within half an hour or one hour, the situation can change a lot. We don't even need to bring in between the moment this witness describes the situation. And the timing of the aerial imagery, if a group of a few hundred people are brought to that field, the situation then looks significantly different. Again, this is an instant shot. Half an hour before, half an hour later, the situation can be different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, to be very correct, you said, on page 72, line 7: "The witness said that at 1400 hours, he saw General Mladic." You know, the correct quotation would be page 70, line 9: "I saw Ratko Mladic coming out of a combat vehicle. That was on the 13th of July, sometime between 1400 hours and 1445 hours." That's slightly different. Be careful if you are quoting something. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We quoted the portion of the statement on page 1383 correctly. The lines were 19 to 25 of that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please don't argue again. When you put your question to the witness, then you made a wrong reference, only to 1400 hours and not 1400 to 1445 hours. This is slightly different, and, therefore, be very correct, please. And now carry on. No discussion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It says here "at 1400 hours and 1430 hours," thank you, and that's how I read it out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, I asked you a moment ago whether these are the only photographs that you received and whether the State Department would give you photographs showing just one small group, not even several hundred people -- not even 200 people, judging by the surface area, and not provide you with photographs where the stadium is full. Thank you. I don't assume that they stopped filming. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is whether there are any more photographs on which he can confirm what he's saying, that later on there were more people, because the witness is claiming here that the stadium was full, whereas Mr. Ruez says that there were as many as are shown on the left-hand photograph in dotted form and they don't take up even one-tenth of the football field, if you look at the scale of the field and the people there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, your question was whether there are any more photographs, and all the other things in the sentences were again a debate. Could you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The answer is simple, is that General Tolimir is wrong when he assumes that the people who took the photograph stopped filming. Again, this is an instant shot. It is not a film. So I am not in a position to discuss the aerial means that enabled the US to take these pictures, but this is, as far as I know, not an extract from a video, it's an instant shot, and that day, in that area, that we only -- material available.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, is it your assessment -- or, rather, how many people would you say there were on the photograph provided to you by the United States of America, the one on the left? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I will not risk to make an assessment just at the top of my head. Trying to do one will require to take very precise measurements, go back to the ground and try to frame precisely the position of these people. And then you have the additional question to know if they are sitting, if they are standing. So I would not be in a position, anyhow, to make a very precise assessment of how many they are at this precise moment on this field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, the rectangle on the US photograph on the left is not a larger surface area than two centimetres' length and one centimetre wide; would that be right? Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would totally disagree, since two centimetres is very far away from the resolution of this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me how many little squares you can fit into the football field? On the empty space of the football field, how many more little squares could you fit in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not make this estimate also on top of my head. I would leave it to you to do it. But this is not part of my concern on this picture. The interest here is to confirm witness testimonies with a photograph that we believe is genuine, and these two things match together. Again, if there is a difference, in terms of numbers that can be seen, the explanation can be that at this day -- moment of that day, the flow of prisoners was continuous, as we could see it on another video on another situation along the asphalt road. So this is again an instant shot. Maybe the field was empty one hour before and full one hour later. This, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Tell us now, please, on what basis do you believe that the situation on the 13th of July, at 1400 hours, on the left-hand side is correct, the one shown by the satellite photograph, the aerial photograph? Why would you say that was correct? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the reason that it matches the parts of the statement of this witness who came here to testify, even though the situation he describes is not exactly the one on the picture, but for the reasons that I already talked about. But it also matches other witness testimonies who might probably not be called just to talk about this, but who were on board of the buses and who could see people getting -- being scrambled on this field, and also due to other informations that we didn't use since they were not on record, but off record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, can this Trial Chamber and this Defence know who those witnesses were? Could we know who those witnesses were, and can we see their statements? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it a question for me or for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There's only one witness present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. In that case, it would need to retake the witness statements and re-identify people who were on board of buses and who we don't necessary interview and even less necessary brought to the Court by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we remain open for any such requests, and we will, in fact, look for such requests for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that offer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if we are presenting evidence here and witness statements, then those witnesses have to be named and they should be accessible to the Defence, because we have to check their authenticity. And that is why I put this question to the witness; namely, who those witnesses were and whether we can obtain that information, whether the Trial Chamber can have that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you didn't listen to the comment of Mr. McCloskey. He said: "We remain open for any such requests, and we will, in fact, look for such requests for the Defence." This is the normal obligation of the OTP, and you may deal in direct contact with the Prosecution. The witness is not in the position to provide you with these documents. Please carry on with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, could you tell us whether there is a big discrepancy in the photograph where the witness indicated and drew what the situation was like at 1400 up until 1430 and the satellite shot that we see of the 13th of July at 1400 hours? Is there a big difference in terms of the surface area that is depicted in one and the other photo? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of numbers, there is certainly a significant difference. But in terms of spotting this place as a regroupment [sic] place for captured prisoners or surrendered people, there is no discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Does this satellite shot actually fix the situation as it was at 1400 hours on the 13th of July, 1995, on this football field? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you object, Mr. McCloskey, I would like -- it's not necessary to object to these questions because the question is already answered, quite clear of the source and the information the witness got from the provider of this aerial photo. Please take into account that the photo on the right side was not taken at the same moment as the photo of the left side. There may be some discrepancies. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the objection is based on the assumption in his question that this is a satellite photo, and the record should reflect in no way his speculations on the platform by which this was taken. That would potentially harm the Rule 70 situation that we have here, and it's my duty, under our Rule 70, to make sure that there aren't speculations or such false issues in the record, is merely what that objection is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, and thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question was, for the witness, whether he could observe a discrepancy between the left-hand photo that was taken from a satellite or in some other way - I don't know what, but it's an aerial photo - and the photograph that was marked by a Prosecution witness who was questioned here on the 26th of April. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already answered that question before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please repeat it for the transcript? Could you just give us a brief answer, yes or no? Can you observe a discrepancy or not? I didn't really get a precise and accurate answer. You tried to explain something, but you didn't actually answer whether you see that there is a discrepancy or a difference between these two photos.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One is in black and white. The other one is in colour. One is seen from an angle roughly west-east. The right one is from an angle north-south. These are differences. Then the other difference, as you already pointed, is the size on this field that was occupied by prisoners. Yes, there is a discrepancy. Where there is no discrepancy is that the witness spots the soccer field of Nova Kasaba as being a regroupment [sic] point for prisoners. He had no photo camera at that time, but the imagery provided by State Department spots prisoners on this soccer field as well. This is the interest of connecting witness testimony with this aerial imagery. But, again, it's an instant shot, so with a little time difference due to the movements of surrendering people that day, within half an hour you can have a very different situation on one spot. It is true here in Nova Kasaba. It is also true for Sandici, exactly for the same reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez. Now, tell us just one more thing: Is there a big difference in the surface area depicting prisoners in the photo as drawn by the witness and the aerial photo, and where can we observe a greater number of prisoners? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think the witness has answered that question several times. You should be a little bit aware on the time you have left today and tomorrow. These are the only days this witness will be present for your cross-examination. Just carry on with other questions. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And on that same subject, Mr. President, I -- as you know, I haven't been doing much redirect, but could I reserve 30 minutes, if possible, for redirect for tomorrow in that same regard? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm sure this is appropriate. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just appreciate it if you take into consideration the fact that the time that was allotted to me was also spent for objections by the Prosecution, and I don't have a problem with objections being made, but I'm just putting questions about the obvious. I haven't put any questions regarding things that are not obvious. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, could you tell us, how far is Sandici from Kasaba or, rather, from this football pitch? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This football pitch is on the line Konjevic Polje at the north and Nova Kasaba at the south. Sandici is on the line that goes from Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac. These are two different areas. If you want a rough estimate of the distance between the two, I would say 13 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please show the witness 65 ter 01450, page 46, and could we at the same time show page 48. Could we have a split screen with the two pages on it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think you need your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We see this field in Sandici, this meadow, and we see Kasaba depicted. The date is 13 July 1995, 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And you said on the transcript that this photograph, where we see a group of people, was taken at the same time, on the 13th of July at 1400 hours. Did I quote you correctly? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two pictures are pictures of Sandici. The picture on the left is, indeed, a picture taken of Sandici precisely the same day and the same hour than the aerial imagery that was taken from Nova Kasaba. But these two spots are the two main regroupment [sic] spots of prisoners, but prisoners who were not in the same area. They were at a distance. Nova Kasaba was the regroupment [sic] spot for the prisoners who had reached this big hill that is just above Konjevic Polje. Sandici is much more towards the east and was the main regroupment [sic] spot for those who had stayed in this area which is nearby Kravica. It's two different spots. But, indeed, the picture of Nova Kasaba and the picture of Sandici, they are from, in fact, the same picture, from the picture of that entire area that day at that hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is this an aerial photo made by the United States?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now a question by Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay. On page 82, line 10 to 12, you state: "Indeed, the picture of Nova Kasaba and the picture of Sandici, they are from, in fact, the same picture, from the picture that entire area that day at that hour." Are you suggesting that the pictures were taken at the same time in Sandici as well as in Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is exactly the same picture, but in such a picture you can go into different areas. This picture covers a very large area, and then you can focus -- if you know where to look into, you can focus on various spots on the same picture. So, in fact, these two pictures are coming from the same picture, the same original picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we are at the end of today's hearing. We have to adjourn. Before we do that, let me make two comments. But, first of all, I would like to thank you, Mr. Ruez. You have to come back tomorrow for a continuation of your examination. And the same advice I gave you the last time; no contact, please, with the Prosecution about this evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Also, just in case, since anyhow Wednesday is a general strike in the country I need to return to, I will have no plane. So if there is absolutely a need for me to testify again on Wednesday, I'm fully at the disposal of the general and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's extremely nice. But, on the other hand, I think there are other witnesses scheduled. No, on Wednesday, we are not sitting. No, no, no, there is no hearing on Wednesday. Next week, and I hope for you there is no strike. Before we adjourn, let me mention the following. Mr. Tolimir, you always have to be aware of the possibility that the Prosecution makes objections. That will be your right as well if the Prosecution is examining any witness. But this is part of the time under your disposal. You should take that into account, and we should try to proceed a little bit faster tomorrow than we did today. The second remark, very shortly. I take it that you withdrew the written motion for receiving two documents; that is, on page 4, line 13 to 15 of today's transcript, the 65 ter 1D81 and 1D82. This motion is withdrawn, and, therefore, there's no need for any decision on that. Thank you very much, and we adjourn until tomorrow at 2.15 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please just -- I'd like to tender this into evidence. I would just like to have the maps that we just saw tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We'll deal with that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of May, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
